newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian official holds talks in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: New Russian official holds talks in Chechnya.

text.p: Boris Berezovsky, the newly appointed deputy secretary of Russia's influential Security Council, met separatist leaders on Sunday in his first trip to the rebel region in his new role.

Itar-Tass news agency said he had met Aslan Maskhadov, the head of an interim coalition government created under a peace deal, in the Chechen capital Grozny to prepare for talks involving Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Tass said the Chechen delegation also included Movladi Udugov, first deputy prime minister of the coalition government, and Culture Minister Akhmed Zakayev. It gave no immediate details of the meeting.

Chernomyrdin has said he is ready to visit Chechnya to boost the peace process but has not set a date for the trip. It would be his first to the southern region since Moscow sent troops to try to smash a drive for independence in December 1994.

Berezovsky's appointment last Tuesday angered the opposition communists, who said the 50-year-old tycoon lacked the experience needed to be on the Security Council, an advisory body of state leaders and security chiefs.
But Tass said the separatists had been impressed with Berezovsky's performance during talks on Saturday in Nazran, just outside Chechnya, which did not cover political issues.

"We saw more pragmatism in Boris Berezovsky's approach to the problem than emotion -- it is emotion which, more than anything, stands in the way of finding a common language," Tass quoted a source in the Chechen delegation as saying.
In his new role, one of Berezovsky's main tasks is expected to be to deal with financial issues connected with the Chechnya crisis.

Fighting has largely halted under the pece deal signed on August 31 but many political problems remain, including arranging regional elections and settling Chechnya's status, either in or out of Russia.

The separatists have been worried that peace efforts could collapse following Yeltsin's sacking last month of Security Council secretary Alexander Lebed, who negotiated the peace agreement and signed it on August 31.
